title: The Moon Unbent
summary: All eight Old Fears slain and Kehlenn's last offer refused: the moon swings back into its old road.

epilogue.title: The Moon Unbent
epilogue.text: The moon straightens out like a bent nail under a hammer, and for the first time in living memory there's a sunrise behind it.

epilogue.title: The Crooked Queen
epilogue.text: Somewhere behind that pale face the Crooked Queen paces a cell made of moonlight, and the tree that held her is ash on the wind.

epilogue.title: Wickermoor Village
epilogue.text: Wickermoor buries its dead and opens its shutters a crack at a time, and the turnip lanterns go back to being just turnips.

epilogue.title: The Green Queen Inn
epilogue.text: The Green Queen pours its first free round the night you come back, and Alda Farnum swears the cellar ghosts have finally gone quiet.

epilogue.title: The Green Queen Inn
epilogue.text: The Green Queen keeps its fire lit through the long dark, and every traveller who stops there hears your names before they hear the menu.

epilogue.title: Mayor Somerton
epilogue.text: Mayor Somerton owns up in front of the whole village to every grave he called an accident, and some say that took more nerve than anything he did before.

epilogue.title: Mayor Somerton
epilogue.text: Mayor Somerton gives a long speech in the square about how he never doubted you, and nobody has the heart to remind him otherwise.

epilogue.title: Constable Squire
epilogue.text: Doris Squire walks the lanes with her lantern every night, and for the first time in years she has nothing to write in her book.

epilogue.title: Mori Shade
epilogue.text: Mori Shade takes down the sign that says no vacancy and sits on his porch a while, which is the closest that man comes to a holiday.

epilogue.title: Sister Rain
epilogue.text: Sister Rain finishes rebuilding the church with her own two hands, and she leaves one window clear so the folk inside can keep an eye on that moon.

epilogue.title: The Crooked House
epilogue.text: Where the Crooked House stood there's only a cellar hole full of rainwater, and the children of Wickermoor dare each other to throw stones in it.

epilogue.title: The Crooked House
epilogue.text: The Crooked House still leans on its hill, empty and sulking, and the village has agreed to look the other way until it falls down on its own.

epilogue.title: Foxwillow
epilogue.text: Foxwillow brings in a harvest with no scarecrow over it, and Jonah gets the windmill turning again by spring.

epilogue.title: Foxwillow
epilogue.text: Foxwillow brings in a harvest with no scarecrow over it, and the farmers leave one row of corn standing for the folk who didn't come home.

epilogue.title: Murkwater Bend
epilogue.text: Down at Murkwater Bend the crossroads shack stands empty, and the bayou folk say the frogs sing a whole lot louder without that ledger on the shelf.

epilogue.title: The Crimson Monastery
epilogue.text: The monastery's bells ring once for every soul Father Renathyr kept, and then they're quiet, and the quiet is a kindness.

epilogue.title: Memory's Rest
epilogue.text: The patients you brought out of Memory's Rest go home to families who'd stopped setting a place for them.

epilogue.title: Skitterdeep
epilogue.text: The plague in the mine town breaks, and the miners go back underground with a new song about the folk who chased the centipede out.

epilogue.title: Skitterdeep
epilogue.text: Skitterdeep counts its graves and goes back to work, the way mining towns always do.

epilogue.title: Maidenmist
epilogue.text: In Maidenmist the dead lie down and stay down, and the groundskeepers finally get to rake the paths in peace.

epilogue.title: The Post Office
epilogue.text: Wickermoor gets a new postmaster, an honest one, and the letters start arriving with nothing in them but news.

epilogue.title: Phillip and Adela
epilogue.text: Folk hang a painting of Phillip and Adela over the inn's hearth, both of them laughing at something just out of frame, the way everybody remembers them.

epilogue.title: What You Carried
epilogue.text: You walked into the dark and came out with clean hands, and there's not a soul in the Hollow who'd say otherwise.

epilogue.title: What You Carried
epilogue.text: You bought your way through with bargains you'd rather not talk about, and on some nights you can still feel the goat's breath on your neck.

epilogue.title: What You Carried
epilogue.text: You struck a bargain or two on the way, the way folk do when the night is long, and you try not to think on the price.

epilogue.title: The Last Ride
epilogue.text: The Ghostlight Express comes whistling out of the mist one more time, and the Vagrant tips his hat and takes your tickets home.
